messages:
devon: :rotating_light: Pager alert RD-OUTAGE-3998 — elevated 502s from prod frontend in eu-west region. saw spike ~12% error rate, user reports from europe. paging network + infra.

pagerduty: Incident triggered: RD-OUTAGE-3998 — High 502 rate in eu-west-1 (alerts from prod-frontend). Pager: devon

mira: @devon looking now. any obvious recent deploys?

devon: no recent deploys. checked pods, none OOMing. health checks show backend returning 502s and a bunch of resets.

ingrid: metrics show the spike started ~18m ago, request latency also increased.

sam: logs: upstreams in eu-central seeing resets from peers in eu-west-1a. traces show requests bouncing between eu-west-1 and eu-central.

devon: that smells like a routing asymmetry — possibly an AZ drain or BGP re-advert. contacting network.

ops-bot: runbook hint: for regional routing loops, try partial traffic-shift + lower DNS TTL + isolate problematic AZ.

devon: lowering DNS TTL from 60 -> 10 for service.redwood-inference.internal to speed up edge convergence. issuing commands:
```
# check current A records
kubectl -n infra exec dns-manager -- dig +short service.redwood-inference.internal @127.0.0.1
# update ttl
kubectl -n infra exec dns-manager -- /usr/local/bin/update-ttl --zone prod --name service --ttl 10
```

mira: I'm starting a controlled traffic-shift away from eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 at 25% to reduce load and break the loop. will watch health.

lia: joining. pulling BGP dumps now, seeing frequent withdraws from aws-eu-west-1a and new AS path prepends from a backup peer. could be fabric instability in that AZ.

devon: as immediate mitigation disabled ECMP on eu-west border peers to force single path and avoid packet spray: `netctl set ecmp eu-west false`

sam: customer impact summary: ~11% of requests returned 502; mostly longer requests >1s or with seq lengths >1024. affected customers: a few enterprise tenants in EU. CS alerted.

ingrid: heatmap shows most of the failures correlate with traffic hitting instances in eu-west-1a specifically.

mira: keeping the 25% shift active. health checks for eu-west backends improved within 10m. error rate fell to ~2%.

lia: planning to cordon and drain the problematic AZ host pool from cloud control plane and then reintroduce after fabric stabilizes. will also request AWS NOC look into link flaps for that AZ.

devon: added temporary header-based routing to prefer eu-central for sticky sessions: header `x-rw-prefer: eu-central` so clients with long-lived connections don't bounce back to eu-west mid-request.

ops-bot: mitigation summary logged: dns ttl lowered to 10s, 25% traffic shift to eu-central, ECMP disabled for eu-west border, problematic AZ pool cordon in progress. Monitor for 15m.

mira: after ~20m of mitigations, 502 rate dropped to 1.2% and p95 latency returned to baseline. continuing watch for full recovery and AWS confirmation.

devon: on-call handover at +45m to mira. handing off: partial shift in place, ttl lowered, ecmp disabled, lia coordinating cloud AZ drain.

mira: ack. i'll own the active monitoring and network follow-ups. lia, please paste the BGP dump when ready.

lia: pasted BGP snippet (abbreviated):
```
> 65001 64512 i 192.0.2.0/24 via 198.51.100.1
  withdraw from 64512 -> repeated withdraw/announce sequence for next 10m
  AS_PATH: 64512 64499 65001 (flapping)
```

sam: support draft for customers ready: brief incident description + mitigations + ETA for postmortem.

devon: timeline notes for postmortem: root cause — AZ fabric instability in eu-west-1a led to BGP withdraws and asymmetric routing; this triggered stuck failover behavior in edge where some clients kept cached routes and were bounced into draining AZ, causing 502s. contributing: short-circuited regional draining logic that didn't verify route convergence, and some clients honoring stale cached paths.

mira: proposed action items: 1) add automated detection for BGP withdraw spikes >X/min and trigger auto-shift, 2) extend regional draining verification to include AS-path convergence checks, 3) documented DNS-ttl adjustment steps in runbook, 4) add observability for ECMP anomalies.

devon: agreed. assigning owners: lia -> BGP detection, ingrid -> draining verification tests, devon -> runbook updates + header-sticky fallback, sam -> customer comms.

ops-bot: Note: incident marked for postmortem. Please attach logs and BGP dumps.

mira: returning to monitoring. error rates stable. I'll keep pager open for 1h then close if no regressions.

devon: closing active mitigation at last_message_ts. final status: resolved. full postmortem to follow. thanks team. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: Incident RD-OUTAGE-3998 resolved — duration 1h13m.

sam: thanks everyone — great coordination. :eyes:
